text: 需要反驳个毛线，全地球发达国家几十个，你想过上现代生活好生活，抄他们作业就行了。
en: There is no need to rebut anything at all; there are dozens of developed countries across the whole planet. If you want to live a modern, good life, just copy their homework.

text: 别整天臆想扩大焦虑和危害，举列子一定要是现实中真实且普遍存在的才有说服力。
en: Do not spend all day imagining and inflating anxiety and harm. The examples you give must be real and commonly found in reality to be persuasive.

text: 人家都这样做肯定是有缘由的，从文艺复兴开始现代化已经几百年，你改开才多久？
en: They all do it this way for a reason. Modernisation has lasted centuries since the Renaissance; how long has your reform and opening-up been going?

text: 你也可以完全按自己乌托邦一样的想法来，不过副作用就是生育率暴跌种族都要灭亡了什么卖淫不卖淫真的还有那么重要吗？
en: You can also go entirely by your own utopian ideas, but the side effect is that the birth rate plummets and the race is on the verge of extinction — at that point, does whether prostitution is legalised or not really matter that much?

text: 还有性是人类根本的欲望，也是精神动力的一分部，你试图通过性专营来压榨男性劳动力，可能刚开始是有用的但是一旦过了某个界线或者灵敏度麻木了，那么整个社会将快速进入低欲望社会，会变得死气沉沉不再充满活力。
en: Moreover, sex is a fundamental human desire and also a part of spiritual drive. If you try to exploit male labour through a sexual monopoly, it may be useful at first, but once a certain boundary is crossed or sensitivity goes numb, the whole society will rapidly enter a low-desire society and become lifeless, no longer full of vitality.

text: 其实我更想看到反驳卖淫合法化的人和彩礼话题下用性服务费+代孕费+保姆费论证高彩礼合理的人先吵一架，当婚姻被解构为购买性服务（实际上并不能保证能买到）的时候再来讨论卖淫合法化总觉得有点儿荒诞。
en: Actually, I would rather see the people who argue against legalising prostitution and the people who, under the bride-price topic, use sex-service fees + surrogacy fees + nanny fees to argue that high bride prices are reasonable have a row first. When marriage is deconstructed as buying sex services (which in reality offers no guarantee you can actually buy any), discussing legalising prostitution afterwards just feels rather absurd.

text: 毕竟传说中妓女很多是禁止接吻要留给男朋友的，这意味着相比彩礼女，你去找个妓女遇到真爱的概率至少不是不存在。
en: After all, legend has it that many prostitutes forbid kissing, saving it for their boyfriends. This means that, compared with bride-price women, your chance of encountering true love by going to a prostitute is at least not non-existent.

text: 买淫合法化这个事情辩论实际上没啥意义，它完全看你是否认同：女人的性比普通劳动更特殊（毕竟男人也没啥性权利）。
en: The debate over legalising prostitution is actually rather pointless; it comes down entirely to whether you accept this: that a woman's sexuality is more special than ordinary labour (after all, men do not have much sexual rights either).

text: 而这个事情本就不是公理，很多地方还有走婚的习俗，你和人家谈卖淫合不合法不搞笑么。
en: Yet this matter is not a self-evident truth to begin with; many places still have the walking-marriage custom. Is it not ridiculous for you to discuss with them whether prostitution is legal or not?

text: 如果你不认同，比如你认为卖淫和脱口秀一样都是第三产业，那么你完全可以说禁止卖淫是对女性的压迫，通过让女性放弃性这一大优赛道转而去和体力占优的男性竞争劳动，降低女性的经济收入从而实现人身依附。
en: If you do not accept it — for instance, if you think prostitution, like stand-up comedy, belongs to the tertiary industry — then you can absolutely say that banning prostitution is oppression of women: by making women give up sex, this major advantageous track, and instead compete in labour with physically superior men, it lowers women's economic income and thereby achieves personal dependence.

text: 大多反对理由本质上都是性不同于劳动这个观点的延伸，比如你为什么不去让你妻子女儿去卖；合法化了以后资本家有的是办法逼你卖；卖会催生黑社会。
en: Most arguments against it are essentially extensions of the view that sex differs from labour — for example, 'why don't you let your wife and daughter go and sell themselves'; 'once it's legalised, capitalists will have no end of ways to force you to sell'; 'selling will breed organised crime'.

text: 你把这几个理由里面的卖替换成劳动是不是感觉变味儿了？
en: If you replace the 'sell' in these arguments with 'labour', doesn't it feel a bit off?

text: 原因就是你认为两者不同。
en: The reason is that you believe the two are different.

text: 你会说有本事你让妻子女儿去上个班？
en: You would say, 'If you've got the ability, let your wife and daughter go to work?'

text: 资本家有的是办法逼我上班，简直坏透了？
en: Capitalists have no end of ways to force me to work — utterly wicked, aren't they?

text: 而黑社会出现的原因本质上政府掌控力缺失，难不成没有黄缅北就会消失么？
en: And the emergence of organised crime is essentially due to a lack of government control. Surely without vice, northern Myanmar would just disappear, would it?

text: 而现在会产生争论的原因就在于，性自由解构婚姻恋爱的同时，也把性的"神圣性"解构了。
en: The reason debate arises now is that sexual freedom, while deconstructing marriage and romance, has also deconstructed the 'sacredness' of sex.

text: 既然可以通过找不爱的人结婚包养来混钱，那零售又差别在哪儿？
en: Since one can marry someone one does not love and be kept for money, where exactly is the difference with retail [prostitution]?

text: 为什么要反驳？
en: Why argue against it?

text: 我支持支持卖因合法化的人可以合法卖因。
en: I support the right of those who support legalising prostitution to legally prostitute themselves.

text: 我不碰，合法化以后也不会去碰。
en: I will not touch it, and will not touch it even after it is legalised.

text: 但是，不反对别人去碰。
en: But I do not object to others touching it.

text: 其实，有些人不是去缓解雌雄异体动物的本能的。
en: Actually, some people are not there to relieve the instinct of dioecious animals.

text: 他可能是去缓解极端焦虑，或极端无聊的，甚至是去释放权力欲的。
en: He may be there to relieve extreme anxiety, or extreme boredom, or even to release a desire for power.

text: ---- 这是一种社会矛盾缓冲地带。
en: ---- This is a buffer zone for social tensions.

text: 合法化以后，反而能阻止各种疾病的传播。
en: Once legalised, it would instead prevent the spread of various diseases.

text: 不止那些人人皆知的病，还有乙肝、衣原体，等等。
en: Not only those widely known illnesses, but also hepatitis B, chlamydia, and so on.

text: 在我看来，一个具有科学思维的时候，就不应该用反驳这类的字眼。
en: In my view, once one possesses scientific thinking, one should not use phrases like 'refute'.

text: 你反驳与否，卖淫现象都客观存在，城市存在，农村存在。
en: Whether you refute it or not, the phenomenon of prostitution exists objectively — in cities, in the countryside.

text: 富人中存在，穷人中也存在。
en: It exists among the rich, and among the poor as well.

text: 人类有文字之前就存在，未来的很久也会存在。
en: It existed before humans had writing, and will exist far into the future.

text: 存在就有存在的原因，限制其存在也有其限制其存在的道理。
en: Where it exists, there is a reason for its existence; restricting its existence also has its own rationale.

text: 说回来说回去还是那句话，关键在于如何改变世界。
en: Going round and round, it still comes to this: the key lies in how to change the world.

text: 在中国，找小三、出轨、包养，给女网友送礼物约炮
en: In China, taking a mistress, having an affair, keeping a lover, sending gifts to female netizens and hooking up

text: 都是不符合道德规范但是不违法的
en: are all against moral norms but not illegal

text: 只有有组织的卖淫才违法
en: only organised prostitution is illegal

text: 所以，国家不是说，张三想花钱曹丕就一点机会都没
en: So the state is not saying that if San Zhang wants to spend money on Pi Cao he has absolutely no chance

text: 真正打击的是，组织规模化的
en: What is truly cracked down on is the organised and scaled [kind]

text: 说句人话就是，如果国家不管
en: To put it plainly, if the state did not intervene

text: 那张小红李小翠王小兰可能就被自己的父亲、老公或者领导恶霸的威逼之下
en: then Xiaohong Zhang, Xiaocui Li and Xiaolan Wang might, under the coercion of their own fathers, husbands or bullying bosses,

text: 自愿卖淫了
en: be 'voluntarily' prostituted

text: 一次，或者一晚是卖淫。
en: Once, or for one night, is prostitution.

text: 是违法。
en: That is illegal.

text: 但是如果我们包月的话，就是包养。
en: But if we do it by the month, it is being kept [as a mistress].

text: 如果不是包的小三的话，其实道德上都不会受到太多谴责对吧？
en: If it is not keeping a mistress, then morally there is not much condemnation, right?

text: 哎，又是羡慕有钱人的一天…
en: Sigh, another day of envying the rich…

text: 你让每个人都活得更加轻松、更加自由、更加有尊严；收入提高、工作压力下降；打击职场欺凌和歧视，打击过度加班和拖欠工资；打击性别歧视、给予弱势群体更多机会；那就不用有人去做（尤其是非自愿、危险的）性工作了。
en: If you let everyone live more easily, more freely, more with dignity; raise incomes and lower work pressure; combat workplace bullying and discrimination, combat excessive overtime and wage arrears; combat gender discrimination and give vulnerable groups more opportunities; then no one would need to do (especially involuntary, dangerous) sex work.

text: 我想请问大家一个问题——什么是卖淫？
en: I would like to ask everyone a question——what is prostitution?

text: 我的理解是，为了金钱，出卖肉体，就是卖淫。
en: My understanding is: selling one's body for money is prostitution.

text: 不管你是说洗脚也好，洗头也好，打着各种旗号，只要是符合这个本质，这种行为就是卖淫。
en: Whether you call it foot-washing or hair-washing, under all manner of banners, as long as it fits this essence, such behaviour is prostitution.

text: 但是如果你这么理解，我觉得现在年轻人谈的所谓的恋爱，恐怕有相当数量实质上都属于卖淫。
en: But if you understand it this way, I think a considerable number of the so-called romances young people talk about nowadays essentially amount to prostitution.

text: 所以其实卖淫早就合法化了。
en: So in fact prostitution was legalised long ago.

text: 在你们还纠结以前的传统模式是不是该受到法律惩罚的时候，其实卖淫早就已经套上了恋爱、婚姻、搭子的外壳，在我们身边各处上演。
en: While you are still agonising over whether the old traditional model should be punished by law, prostitution has long since put on the guise of romance, marriage and companionship, playing out all around us.

text: 只是太多人没有发现或者不愿意承认而已。
en: It is just that too many people have not noticed, or are unwilling to admit it.

text: 反驳不了，不管是逻辑上还是事实上都站不住脚。
en: It cannot be refuted; it does not hold up, whether logically or factually.

text: B站上法山叔就这个事出过一个视频，名字叫“性交易的违法成本，对有的人重如泰山，对有的人轻如鸿毛”，出错啦! - bilibili.com里面讲的应该挺全面了，
en: On Bilibili, Uncle Shan Fa made a video about this, titled “The cost of illegality for sex transactions: as heavy as Mount Tai to some, as light as a goose feather to others” — oops, a mistake! - bilibili.com — what it covers should be fairly comprehensive,

text: 知乎上大多数人的法律素质应该是比不上这个UP的。
en: Most people's legal literacy on Zhihu is probably no match for this UP.

text: 我不支持卖淫合法，我也不止持色情业合法。
en: I do not support legalising prostitution, nor do I support legalising the sex industry.

text: 但我想问问那些左棍，你们的群体为什么不允许机器人带性器官啊?请问是剥削了机器人还是剥削了代码?请问是机器人性不同意还是代码有自由意志?
en: But I want to ask those lefties: why does your group not allow robots to have sexual organs? May I ask, are you exploiting the robot or exploiting the code? May I ask, does the robot not consent sexually, or does the code have free will?

text: 他们就不知道性病这种病吗？
en: Don't they know about diseases like STDs?

text: 无知者无畏啊。
en: The ignorant know no fear.

text: 看了这么多回答，唯一在情感上让我赞同的是“黄往往涉黑，为了打击黑，所以要扫黄”的观点，很多答主无论是现身说法，还是让我们换位思考，都很富有感染力，但是这个观点并不能完全说服我。
en: Having read so many answers, the only view I emotionally agree with is 'vice often involves organised crime, so to strike at crime we must sweep vice'. Many answerers, whether speaking from personal experience or asking us to see things from others' perspectives, are very persuasive, but this view does not fully convince me.

text: “黄往往涉黑”，可是只要有反例就可以推翻这个观点，但凡有一定了解的，性交易不当然存在鸡头，个体户是有的。
en: 'Vice often involves organised crime' — yet this view can be overturned by a single counterexample. Anyone with some understanding knows that sex transactions do not inevitably involve a pimp; there are independent operators.

text: 以“黄往往涉黑”认为需要扫黄的朋友们，我想问一下，为什么在抓嫖的时候不再审查一下这个卖淫女是个体户还是有组织的？
en: Friends who argue for sweeping vice on the basis of 'vice often involves organised crime', I would like to ask: when arresting clients, why not also vet whether the prostitute is an independent operator or part of an organisation?

text: 即便有组织，为什么不再审查一下这个组织到底是否存在压迫呢？
en: Even if there is an organisation, why not vet whether that organisation actually involves oppression?

text: 不说实践了，甚至立法都没有在这上面做区分。
en: Not to mention practice — even legislation makes no such distinction.

text: 如果立法上都一刀切了，实践只会更片面（这不是危言耸听，）我知道又有人拿审查成本说事儿，但是一刀切就意味着误伤，就意味着不涉黑、完全基于自由意志、各取所需的性交易被公权力粗暴地禁止了，若是扫黄是因为可能涉黑，那禁止不涉黑的黄符合你们的观点吗？
en: If legislation takes a blanket approach, practice will only be even more one-sided (this is no alarmism). I know someone will again bring up the cost of vetting, but a blanket approach means collateral damage — it means sex transactions that involve no organised crime, are based entirely on free will and are mutually beneficial get crudely banned by public power. If sweeping vice is because it might involve organised crime, then does banning vice that involves no organised crime fit your view?

text: 你们说黄可能涉黑，那打击涉黑的黄岂不更好？
en: You say vice may involve organised crime, so wouldn't it be better to strike at the vice that involves organised crime?

text: 穆勒在《论自由》里提到，公民的任何行为如果仅涉己身，那他享有完全的自由，公众或公权力对他们自甘堕落或其他不符合自身价值观的行为可以加以劝诱、表达自己的不满、对此人疏远，但谴责、禁止是不必的。
en: Mill, in On Liberty, mentions that if any citizen's behaviour concerns only themselves, they enjoy complete freedom. The public or public power may persuade, express dissatisfaction, or distance themselves from those who degrade themselves or act against their own values, but condemnation and prohibition are unnecessary.

text: 公权力的界限由此划分。
en: Thus the boundary of public power is drawn.

text: 所以，支持性交易合法化不是说支持身边的女儿、妻子去做性交易，而是捍卫卖淫女选择一种不涉他人的生存途径的自由。
en: Therefore, supporting the legalisation of sex transactions is not about supporting one's own daughter or wife engaging in sex transactions, but about defending the prostitute's freedom to choose a livelihood that involves no one else.

text: 至少从涉黑的角度，没有强有力的理由禁止 。
en: At least from the angle of organised crime, there is no strong reason to prohibit it.

text: 还有观点认为性交易对青少年存在不良引导。
en: Another view holds that sex transactions exert a bad influence on teenagers.

text: 这点穆勒也在《论自由》里提到了，他认为法律赋予了父母、国家和公序良俗长达十多年时间的权力（就是权力）对孩子的心智进行塑造，如果孩子被不文明的事物引导堕落，那只能归责于教育者和自身的秉性，只能认为是捍卫自由必要的社会成本。
en: On this point Mill also mentions in On Liberty that he believes the law grants parents, the state and public decency more than a decade of power (yes, power) to shape a child's mind. If a child is led astray by uncivilised things, blame can only fall on the educator and the child's own disposition; it can only be regarded as the social cost necessary to defend freedom.

text: 另外，既然文明在野蛮横行的年代战胜了野蛮，为何要害怕野蛮在文明广泛的世界取缔文明？
en: Moreover, since civilisation triumphed over barbarism in an age when barbarism ran rampant, why fear that barbarism will abolish civilisation in a world where civilisation is widespread?

text: 在我看来，唯一称得上性交易合法化的阻碍的，有且仅有公序良俗，因为任何一个人只要提出性交易合法化，甚至将该提议做成提案上交到人大，都会被公众千夫所指（没有说公众不好的意思，刚才也说了，公众对自己不喜欢的有反对的自由），最后不了了之。
en: In my view, the only thing that can truly be called an obstacle to legalising sex transactions is, and is only, public order and good morals. For as soon as anyone proposes legalising sex transactions, or even turns the proposal into a bill submitted to the National People's Congress, they will be condemned by the public (I am not saying the public is bad — as I said, the public has the freedom to oppose what it dislikes), and it ends up coming to nothing.
